propositions: Op-cert per-job boto3/SSM/region lookup couples app config to one secret store and creates concurrency/cleanup hazards; startup binding must move key acquisition to initialization before queue/worker/network/workspace creation.

Exactly one of REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH or REBAR_OPCERT_PRIVATE_KEY must be accepted at startup with validation (presence, readability, file permissions 0600-or-stricter, Ed25519 format) and copied to a process-owned 0700 dir/0600 file that never modifies the deployment source.

Both out-of-opcert_service/ producer chains (completion: transition_close.py:sign_completion_verdict→signing.sign_manifest; plan-review: attest.py→generation.sign_manifest via _sign_manifest_under_lock→mint_opcert_record) must accept and forward an optional context-local OpcertSigner binding, decoupling mint_opcert_record and sign_manifest from os.environ while preserving env/genesis resolution for developer-local callers.
Concurrent and timed-out jobs must prove context-local signer/principal/push isolation with one immutable startup signer, no workspace push remote, and no mutual state observation or mutation.

Op-cert application runtime (src/rebar/opcert_service) must have zero SSM/boto3/AWS_REGION runtime dependency; the key is materialized outside the app by fetch-secrets.sh to a 0600 file and bind-mounted :ro with REBAR_OPCERT_KEY_PATH, while the shared /rebar/prod/* SSM grant in iam.tf remains unchanged.
Secret/key material must not appear in repr, serialization, argv, logs, exceptions, output, fingerprints, provenance, or persisted envelopes beyond the existing public signature.
